query: What spatial resolution and synchronization frequency were used to assimilate ocean observations into the digital twin?
draft_answer: The provided evidence does not identify a specific spatial resolution used to assimilate ocean observations into a digital twin; one paper explicitly says no spatial resolution is given, and another notes only that ocean observations are used alongside historical and forecast data without specifying assimilation resolution [https://openalex.org/W4387452406||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4367611274||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4367611274||ABSTRACT||001]. Similarly, the evidence does not provide a numerical synchronization frequency for assimilation: one summary says digital twins are synchronized with their real-world counterparts at a “specific frequency and fidelity,” but no frequency is stated [https://openalex.org/W4367611274||ABSTRACT||000]. Another source similarly reports that only general barriers in spatial coverage and temporal resolution are discussed, not an actual synchronization schedule [https://openalex.org/W4387452406||ABSTRACT||000]. A separate paper on a GNSS buoy for estuarine and coastal water-surface elevation monitoring reports the sensing and transmission setup, but it does not mention digital-twin assimilation, spatial resolution, or synchronization frequency [pmc_PMC5298745||ABSTRACT||000]. Taken together, the evidence supports only a general description of digital-ocean-twin data use and synchronization, not the exact resolution or update rate requested [https://openalex.org/W4367611274||ABSTRACT||000] [https://openalex.org/W4387452406||ABSTRACT||000].
